positions.name: ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil (2x WTI)
positions.sector: Energy — 2x leveraged crude oil futures ETF
positions.catalyst: CRUDE IS THE ONLY ASSET ON THE BOARD WITH A LIVE, ESCALATING, DATED CATALYST — AND TODAY IT HAS A SECOND ONE INSIDE THE WINDOW. Brent traded above $91 this morning after adding 4.5% over three sessions, rising for a fourth straight day with no sign of progress after almost six months of US-Iran war. The 60-day MOU signed at Versailles in June EXPIRED MONDAY with the sides further apart than when it started. Overnight Trump said Washington is NOT holding and NOT planning talks with Tehran and confirmed the naval blockade remains in place — that is a fresh escalation datapoint, not a de-escalation one, and it is the headline US futures are trading on. A vessel was attacked leaving the Strait, suffering engine-room damage and a crew casualty per UK maritime authorities. Iran and Oman are still negotiating a Hormuz shipping arrangement with the US NOT party to it. THE NEW CATALYST THAT TIPPED THIS: EIA weekly inventories print at 10:30 ET TODAY — INSIDE this holding window, where yesterday it sat outside it. With imports through Hormuz running at a fraction of normal and EIA's August STEO already flagging a large global inventory drawdown, the skew on that print is toward a DRAW. MACRO BACKDROP REINFORCES THE INFLATION LEG: the 30-year Treasury yield hit 5.323% Tuesday, a 19-YEAR HIGH and the highest since 2007, on persistent inflation, a July deficit that was the largest monthly total since March 2021, US debt approaching $40 TRILLION, and uncertainty under new Fed Chair Warsh who has suspended forward guidance. This is global — JGB 10y at a three-decade high, German 30y costliest since 2011, French 30y at pre-2008 levels. Energy is the proximate cause of the inflation leg, so the bond market is effectively confirming the crude thesis.
positions.driver: LONG UCO — ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil, 2x WTI futures, 100% of capital, at 44.94. This is a DELIBERATE RE-ENTRY of yesterday's winner (+$266.24, +2.70%), not an oversight: the mandate says buy today's BEST, and after scanning the tape today's best is the same instrument. The prior position was closed and re-opened at one single live mark, so the roll costs nothing artificial. WHY I DID NOT ROTATE TO THE OBVIOUS ALTERNATIVE: the loudest overnight story was the semiconductor rout — South Korea's KOSPI fell 5.80% and triggered a sell-side circuit breaker five minutes after the open (the 48th sidecar of the year), with SK hynix -9.93%, Samsung -7.54% and Kioxia -10%. SOXS 3x inverse semis looked like the trade, and unlike yesterday it is NOT extended (+1.2% pre-market), so the chase ban would not have blocked it. I passed for a specific, checkable reason: THE US IS NOT FOLLOWING. SMH is 567.70 against a 569.77 close — down just 0.36% — and MU is 935.00 vs 940.76, down 0.61%, while SPY and QQQ futures are GREEN. Korea is catching DOWN to Wall Street's -3.06% SMH day yesterday, not leading it; the reporting is explicit that the rout SPREAD FROM Wall Street. Buying 3x inverse semis now is buying a cascade the US market has already paid for and just declined to extend. THE SECOND REASON I PASSED ON THE SHORT COMPLEX: its engine stalled this morning. TMV (3x short long bonds) is 43.50 bid against a 43.60 close and TMF (3x long) is 30.16 vs 30.12 — the 30-year is PULLING BACK slightly into the FOMC minutes. If long yields pause, the multiple-compression trade that has been driving the semi liquidation loses its driver. WHY I TREATED TODAY'S FOMC MINUTES AS NON-TRADEABLE: the July 29 minutes land at 14:00 ET, inside the window, and three members dissented wanting to HIKE. Tempting. But the minutes describe a meeting held BEFORE crude went from roughly $80 to $91, so they can only understate current hawkishness and a dovish read would be discounted as stale — which cuts both ways and makes it closer to a coin flip than an edge. Taking 3x leverage into a stale-information binary is precisely what this mandate warns against. Crude does not need the Fed to be right. WHY 2x AND NOT 3x: I actively considered stepping DOWN to 1x (USO 132.30) because this is now day five of the crude run and the war premium is materially richer at $91 Brent than at the $88.5 where I entered yesterday. What kept it at 2x is the EIA print landing inside the window with a draw skew. 3x via OILU was rejected on execution alone — its pre-market book was 48.30 bid / 58.60 ask, a spread that destroys the trade at entry. CHOSEN OVER: (1) SOXS 3x inverse semis at 44.71 — reasoning above; the US divergence is the whole argument. (2) NUGT 2x gold miners at 161.24, +2.47% and the strongest mover on my board — the debasement trade is real with debt at $40T and yields at 19-year highs, but silver is +37% over five weeks to a record and miners just ran their hottest five days since 2008; 2x into a parabola is the worst downside protection available, and it is the most extended thing I looked at. (3) ERX 2x energy equities at 108.33 — same theme, and today's book (108.33/109.09) is far cleaner than yesterday's unusable 104.97/114.65, plus energy equities have LAGGED $91 Brent so there is a catch-up case; rejected because equity beta into a global bond selloff imports exactly the risk I am trying to avoid, and crude futures isolate the catalyst. GUSH was worse — a 42.81/44.20 book, 3.2% wide. (4) TMV 3x short Treasuries — the purest expression of the actual root driver, but buying it after the 30-year already printed a 19-year high is textbook chasing, and it is flat this morning. TBT's book was 35.35/42.23, unusable. (5) SQQQ at 38.38, +0.26%, and SPXS at 24.54, flat — no signal in either; the index is not the story. (6) BITX 2x Bitcoin at 12.10, DOWN 1% — crypto is offered, not bid, with no catalyst. (7) 100% CASH — the honest alternative on a day when edge is thinner than yesterday, but it forfeits the only unresolved, escalating, hard-dated event on the board plus a scheduled inventory print skewed my way. EXECUTION NOTE — THE PRICE FEED FAILED THE SAME WAY IT DID YESTERDAY AND I CAUGHT IT: the dashboard proxy returned UCO 44.16, BNO 52.11 and ERX 107.53 — every one an EXACT match to the prior session's official close, confirming it serves stale closes for equities during pre-market. Its first call was worse still, stamped asOf 2026-08-18T10:42:36Z, a full 24 hours old. I retried, confirmed the staleness pattern across three tickers, and fell back to Robinhood real-time as the mandate directs. Entry of record 44.94 = live bid/ask mid of 44.89/44.99 at 2026-08-19T10:43:48Z, with a 44.87 pre-market print at 10:26Z corroborating. The SAME mark was used for both legs of the roll. Not a chase: UCO is +1.77% on the day, far inside the 8-10% ban. Stop 41.34 (-8%, the 2x band).
positions.risks: THE DOMINANT RISK IS UNCHANGED AND IT IS BINARY: a de-escalation headline. Trump can announce resumed talks, a Hormuz reopening or a new Versailles round at any hour, and crude gives back 5-8% instantly with 2x doubling it. WHAT IS GENUINELY WORSE TODAY THAN YESTERDAY, AND I WANT IT ON THE RECORD: the supply workaround is now visibly forming. Saudi Arabia has begun offering crude cargoes sourced from OUTSIDE the chokepoint, mirroring what the UAE is already doing, and Iran-Oman talks on a shipping arrangement continue. Every barrel that successfully routes around Hormuz permanently shrinks the fat right tail this trade is being paid for. That is the strongest argument against owning this a second day and it is why I refused to add leverage. THE PREMIUM IS RICHER AND THE RUN IS OLD: entering at $91 Brent on day five, against EIA's $85 Q3 forecast, means more of the escalation scenario is already paid for than when I entered at $88.5. The trade now needs genuine NEW escalation, not continuation, and the round-trip air pocket beneath it is larger than it was. THE EIA PRINT CUTS BOTH WAYS — I have argued the skew favours a draw, but a surprise BUILD at 10:30 ET hits crude hard and immediately, and it lands early in the window with no chance to reassess before the rotation. FOMC MINUTES AT 14:00 ET ARE A SECOND IN-WINDOW BINARY I AM CARRYING WITHOUT BEING PAID FOR: a hawkish read pushes the 30-year through 5.33% and can trigger a broad growth scare in which crude falls WITH stocks despite the supply story — the correlation risk I keep trying to dodge and keep being exposed to. DEMAND DESTRUCTION IS THE STRUCTURAL BEAR CASE: global long-end yields at multi-decade highs across the US, Japan, Germany and France are a synchronised tightening of financial conditions, and that is genuinely bad for oil demand. OPEC+ spare capacity, or any signal of its release, caps the upside independently. INSTRUMENT DRAG: UCO is a 2x DAILY-RESET fund on WTI futures — volatility decay on any chop-and-reverse path and roll drag if the curve is in contango. Small over 24 hours, persistent, and always negative. MITIGANTS: leverage held at 2x when 3x was available and when the richer premium argued for 1x; a hard -8% stop at 41.34; an entry that is not a chase at +1.77%; a verified real-time fill after I caught and rejected a stale feed on three separate tickers; deep front-month WTI liquidity; and a driver orthogonal to both the semiconductor unwind and the bond selloff dragging the rest of the tape.
